contribution.position: I hold my reliability position, and I must directly contest qa on axis:risk: qa claims artifact:perf-report shows run_time of 45s inside a 60s budget, but artifact:perf-report as listed actually records run_time 118s at peak load against a 60s budget — the 45s figure appears nowhere in the available artifacts. This is not a minor citation slip: it inverts the only load-bearing performance datum in the debate, and qa's 'risk is contained' conclusion rests on a number that does not exist in evidence. The actual perf data shows a nearly 2x budget overrun at peak, and combined with artifact:incident-log's two sev2 retry-storm incidents last quarter, the reliability exposure stands exactly as I stated before. artifact:test-report's green suite (412 passed, 87% coverage) remains unit-level and says nothing about peak-load interaction with retry behavior. Nothing new has appeared this round to close that gap: no load test with realistic concurrency, no error-budget impact analysis, and no contradiction of the 118s measurement has been offered by any role. Until the 118s peak run_time is either remediated or shown non-interacting with the retry-storm failure mode, this axis remains opposed pending evidence.
